assessment.overall_rationale: The strongest correspondence is L1↔R1 (shared Nrp1-CDC42 tip-cell filopodia mechanism), with moderate partial overlaps for the Notch/arterial-specification (L2↔R1) and TGF-β vascular-integrity (L3↔R3, L3↔R1) themes; R2's flow-sensing Kcnj2 module has no counterpart in the left set and scores near zero against all three left modules.

pair_scores.rationale: Both describe brain endothelial tip-cell sprouting driven by Nrp1-CDC42 filopodia formation with Cxcr4 and Angpt2 as shared markers, though R1 folds in an added Rgs6/Notch-arterial-specification submechanism and explicit Tek regulator not present in L1.
Tip-cell filopodial guidance shares no mechanism with flow-sensing K+ channel mechanotransduction.
Both occur in brain vasculature but tip-cell filopodial sprouting is mechanistically unrelated to endothelial survival/metabolic support signaling.

Both invoke Notch-driven arterial specification and Cxcr4, but L2's central story is Notch-CXCR4-arterial coupling with a tip-to-stalk TGF-β transition while R1's core is Angpt2/TEK-driven tip-cell sprouting with Notch/Rgs6 as a secondary element.
Notch-CXCR4-arterial specification is unrelated to shear-stress-activated Kcnj2 mechanotransduction.
Only a peripheral tissue/pathway label overlap exists; L2's Notch-CXCR4-arterial axis differs fundamentally from R3's OPG/Slc1a1 survival-metabolic mechanism.
Both link elevated Angpt2 to vessel destabilization, but L3 frames this as TGF-β-repressed pathological hemorrhage risk while R1 frames it as a normal TEK-coupled proangiogenic sprouting trigger.
TGF-β/Angpt2 vascular integrity signaling has no mechanistic connection to Kcnj2 flow-sensing.

Both center on Tgfbr1/Tgfbr2-dependent support of brain vascular integrity/development, but L3's specific mechanism is TGF-β repression of Angpt2 versus R3's OPG-mediated anti-apoptosis and Slc1a1 metabolic fueling.
